about.title: Winters Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Winters is a small, walkable town, but that doesn't mean its sidewalks, parking lots, and business floors are always free of hazards. A wet floor near Grant Avenue shops, a broken step outside an older downtown building, or uneven pavement along County Road 89 can cause a serious fall in an instant. Under California law, proving a property owner's fault usually means showing they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why documenting the scene, taking photos of the exact hazard, and requesting any nearby surveillance footage matters early. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice or represent you directly. Instead, we connect injured Winters residents and visitors with an independent attorney from our network who can evaluate the fall, gather evidence, and explain your options, all without any upfront cost to you.

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Quickly
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Winters shop or lot is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting fast to preserve it can make the difference in a premises liability claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery, just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help present the facts fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Winters?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a City of Winters building or sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. It's worth having an attorney review the details as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell but didn't take photos at the time?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not necessarily fatal to a claim. An attorney can still request incident reports, surveillance video if it still exists, and witness statements from the business or property owner. The sooner this happens after a fall near Grant Avenue or elsewhere in Winters, the better the chances of preserving useful evidence.

items.question: Does LawProactive represent me in my case?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't provide legal representation or advice. We match you with an independent attorney in our network who can review your Winters fall and handle the case on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless you recover.
